note: Coverage of the registries that are coded for the conditions this site describes, outside France. The French registries are drawn département by département in registry-zones.json from the Santé publique France surveillance report. Registries with status "clinical" are not population-based: they recruit through participating hospitals rather than covering a territory, so their outline marks the country they work in and claims no coverage of the births in it. Status "hospital" marks a national system that samples births through reporting hospitals rather than covering every birth in a territory. Entries with "map": false are registries this register lists without drawing: an umbrella with no territory of its own, a hospital network, a single centre, or a national register we cite without having mapped its coverage. Status "study" marks a population-based study built on registries, listed because papers in our bibliography rest on it; it covers no territory and is not drawn. Each entry's "match" phrases are what tools/enrich-bibliography-registries.py looks for in a paper's title and abstract to record that the paper rests on the registry. "source" carries the full provenance and "source_short" a one-line citation; the map popup shows the short one, because a popup that quotes four references is unreadable and the registries page carries them in full. "since" is the year the registry itself started collecting, not the year it joined a network, and each entry's source says where the year comes from. An entry without it is one whose start year we have not sourced; the card leaves the line out rather than guessing. "label" is the registry's official title and nothing else: no city, country or operating body appended, because the area, country and kind fields carry those. "local" holds the official title in the registry's own language where that is not English. An entry is listed when the registry shows data from 2022 or later, or appears in the current EUROCAT member list or ICBDSR programme directory. "geounit" draws a whole nation of the United Kingdom from Natural Earth's geonunit field. "since" holds a year only, because the map reads it as "Collecting since"; "since_note" keeps the detail behind that year.

areas.label: Hunan Birth Defects Surveillance System
areas.area: 52 registered surveillance hospitals in Hunan; 847,755 births in 2016-2020
areas.kind: Hospital-based surveillance run by the Hunan Provincial Health Commission; fetuses and births with birth defects are reported from registered hospitals.
areas.source: 'Epidemiology of congenital polydactyly and syndactyly in Hunan Province, China', BMC Pregnancy Childbirth 2024 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10960469/ (read: system, 52 hospitals, 847,755 births). areas.source_short: BMC Pregnancy Childbirth 2024 (PMC10960469)
areas.since_note: not established (data from 2010 in a 2010-2020 analysis)

areas.label: Japan Environment and Children's Study
areas.area: 104,102 infants enrolled at 15 regional centres across Japan (pregnancies recruited January 2011 to March 2014)
areas.kind: Nationwide birth cohort; congenital anomalies are transcribed from medical records at delivery and one month by trained staff on a list of 61 anomalies.
areas.source: Prevalence of Congenital Anomalies in the Japan Environment and Children's Study, J Epidemiol 2019 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6556438/ (read). 2024 follow-up seen in a search engine listing https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/ehpm/29/0/29_23-00366/_article (not read).
areas.source_short: J Epidemiol 2019 (PMC6556438)

areas.label: Cambodia Mine/ERW Victim Information System
areas.area: Cambodia, national: 65,125 explosive ordnance casualties recorded January 1979 to December 2025, of whom 9,101 amputated
areas.kind: Casualty and victim database set up in 1994 by the Cambodian Red Cross with Handicap International Belgium and UNICEF, fully managed by the Cambodian Mine Action and Victim Assistance Authority since 2009; data gatherers interview local authorities, mine action agencies, families and casualties.
areas.source: CMVIS monthly report on explosive ordnance accidents, December 2025 https://www.cmaa.gov.kh/assets/cmvis/12-cmvis-monthly-report-for-dec-2025-(eng).pdf (read via pdftotext).
areas.source_short: CMAA CMVIS monthly report, December 2025

areas.label: National Congenital Anomaly and Rare Disease Registration Service (England)
areas.area: England, all pregnancies with a congenital condition; the 2022 report describes babies born or delivered in 2022 (about 255 affected per 10,000 total births, one in 39)
areas.kind: National population-based registry of congenital anomalies and rare diseases, run within NHS England (National Disease Registration Service), which finds cases through hospital, laboratory and screening sources.
areas.url_status: 403, checked 22 November 2026 (the site refuses automated checks)
areas.source: GOV.UK, NCARDRS congenital anomaly official statistics report 2022, https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/ncardrs-congenital-anomaly-official-statistics-report-2022 (read: 2022 data, published 23 October 2025). EUROCAT member list, https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries_en?page=2 (read: England NCARDRS is a full member). a search engine excerpt for the NHS Digital 2022 report page gave the 255.0 per 10,000 figure; that page returned HTTP 403 and was not read directly.
areas.source_short: GOV.UK NCARDRS 2022 statistics (23 Oct 2025); EUROCAT member list
areas.since_note: 2015 as NCARDRS (continues the earlier regional BINOCAR registers)

areas.label: Congenital Anomaly Register and Information Service for Wales
areas.area: All of Wales, about 35,000 births a year
areas.kind: Population-based register hosted by Public Health Wales, with multi-source case finding (antenatal clinics, delivery units, paediatric and orthopaedic services, cytogenetics, pathology, regional surgery centres).
areas.source: EUROCAT registry page for Wales, https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries/wales_en (area, births, start 1998, sources). gov.wales, CARIS annual report 1998-2025 release page, https://www.gov.wales/congenital-anomaly-register-and-information-service-caris-annual-report-1998-2024 (release 10 November 2026, data 1998-2025). CARIS annual report 2024 PDF, https://beta-phw.nhs.wales/app/uploads/sites/2/2026/04/CARIS-annual-report-2024.pdf (read as text: data 1998-2024, 745 cases registered for 2024, limb anomalies among main groups).
areas.source_short: EUROCAT Wales page; gov.wales CARIS 2025 release; CARIS annual report 2024

areas.label: Congenital and Rare Conditions Registry Service for Scotland
areas.area: All of Scotland: pregnancies ending in Scotland to resident mothers, about 1,100 affected babies a year (1,102 in 2024, 239.2 per 10,000 total births)
areas.kind: National register maintained by Public Health Scotland, with inclusion following EUROCAT criteria; it replaces the interim linked dataset SLiCCD from 2021.
areas.source: Public Health Scotland, Congenital conditions in Scotland, https://publichealthscotland.scot/publications/congenital-anomalies-in-scotland (read: release 27 October 2026, 2021-2024 data, 1,102 babies in 2024). EUROCAT member list, https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries_en?page=3 (read: CARDRISS register full member). EUROCAT SLiCCD page, https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/node/1204_pl (start 2000, 48,000-60,000 births a year, linked sources).
areas.source_short: Public Health Scotland CARDRISS release (27 Oct 2026); EUROCAT member list
areas.since_note: Register launched 2023; the SLiCCD linked dataset covers pregnancies from 2000

areas.label: EUROCAT Funen registry of congenital anomalies (Odense, Funen)
areas.local: Fyns Amts register over medfødte misdannelser
areas.area: Island of Funen and surrounding small islands, about 5,600 births a year in three hospitals
areas.kind: Population-based registry run from the paediatric department of Lillebaelt Hospital, Kolding; includes live births, fetal deaths from 20 weeks and terminations after prenatal diagnosis.
areas.source: EUROCAT member list, https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries_en (read: Denmark Funen, full member). EUROCAT Funen history page, https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/node/123_it (read: area, 1979, 5,600 births, update 1 March 2023). Frontiers in Pediatrics 2021 paper on multiple anomalies 1990-2014, https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fped.2021.614864 (named in a search engine listing, not read).
areas.source_short: EUROCAT member list and Funen history page

areas.label: Greenland congenital anomaly surveillance (EUROCAT affiliate)
areas.area: All of Greenland, about 800 births a year (national hospital, 4 regional hospitals and 5 of 12 health care centres)
areas.kind: Population-based surveillance with compulsory case notification by hospitals and active case finding in discharge diagnoses, hospital records, birth notifications, death certificates and laboratory data.
areas.source: EUROCAT member list page 4, https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries_en?page=3 (read: Denmark, Greenland, affiliate member). EUROCAT Greenland page, https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries/greenland_en (read: area, births, 1979 and 1983, sources).
areas.source_short: EUROCAT member list and Greenland registry page
areas.since_note: 1979 (national registry); general anomaly surveillance including Greenland since 1983

areas.label: Styrian Malformation Registry (EUROCAT Styria)
areas.local: Steirisches Fehlbildungsregister
areas.area: Province of Styria (about 19.5 per cent of Austria), about 10,000 births a year, 13 per cent of Austrian births
areas.kind: Population-based registry at the Medical University of Graz, fed by hospital patient records, the human genetics institute and pathology charts; about half of the cases come from more than one source.
areas.source: EUROCAT member list page 1, https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries_en (read: Austria Styria, full member). EUROCAT Styria page, https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries/styria_en (read: area, births, 1986, sources, update 17.04.2023).
areas.source_short: EUROCAT member list and Styria registry page

areas.label: Mainz Model, birth defects monitoring of Mainz and Rheinhessen (EUROCAT Mainz)

areas.area: Mainz district and Rheinhessen, about 370,000 inhabitants and 3,300 births a year in three maternity hospitals; non-residents excluded
areas.kind: Population-based monitoring in which paediatricians examine each newborn in the first week, with pathology and prenatal diagnosis data for stillbirths and terminations.
areas.source: EUROCAT member list page 5, https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries_en?page=4 (read: Germany Mainz, affiliate member). Bundesaerztekammer note on birth defect registers, https://www.bundesaerztekammer.de/fileadmin/user_upload/BAEK/Themen/Medizin_und_Ethik/Begleitartikel_SN_Fehlbildungen_FINAL.pdf (named in a search engine listing only).
areas.source_short: EUROCAT member list and Mainz registry page

areas.label: SwedeAmp, the Swedish Amputation and Prosthetics Registry
areas.local: Svenskt amputations- och protesregister
areas.area: Sweden, national quality registry; 17 of 21 regions and 36 of 67 hospitals take part, covering 48.6 per cent of initial lower limb amputations in 2018-2023
areas.kind: National quality registry for lower limb amputation and prosthetic care, funded by the Swedish Association of Local Authorities and Regions, with Region Skane as data controller; follows patients at 6, 12 and 24 months.
areas.source: Evaluation of the SwedeAmp database, Canadian Prosthetics and Orthotics Journal 7(2), November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11844758/ (read: 2018-2023, 5,246 of 10,788 amputations, 17 of 21 regions, start 2011, lower limb only). Swedish Association of Local Authorities and Regions registry archive page, https://skr.se/en/kvalitetsregister/hittaregister/registerarkiv/amputationochprotes.44126.html (named in a search engine listing; returned 404 on 22 November 2026).
areas.source_short: Canadian Prosthetics and Orthotics Journal, Nov 2024 (SwedeAmp coverage)

areas.label: Danish Amputation Database (DanAmp)
areas.local: Dansk Amputationsdatabase
areas.area: Denmark, national; 11 of 21 departments performing major lower-extremity amputations were entering data, seven more in talks
areas.kind: Clinical quality database set up by a steering committee with all five Danish regions; surgeons enter data on surgery and later events, with patient questionnaires at 3, 6, 12, 24 and 36 months and written consent.
areas.source: Danish Amputation Database article, Danish Medical Journal 2025, https://ugeskriftet.dk/dmj/danish-amputation-database (read: start 2022, 11 of 21 departments, outcome questionnaires, lower limb only, published 22 July 2025).
areas.source_short: Dan Med J 72(8), July 2025 (DanAmp validity study)

areas.label: Amputation Registry Germany (AMP-Registry), pilot in Baden-Wuerttemberg
areas.local: Amputationsregister Deutschland (AMP-Register)
areas.area: Pilot phase: Heidelberg study centre plus seven providers and centres in Baden-Wuerttemberg; 712 datasets collected, 498 in the first analysis
areas.kind: Registry run by the Medical-Technical Competence Centre for Orthopaedic Technology (Heidelberg university orthopaedic clinic with Fraunhofer IPA), funded by the state of Baden-Wuerttemberg from 2021.
areas.source: Update of the Amputation Registry Germany (AMP-Registry), Unfallchirurgie 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11933216/ (read: MeTKo Heidelberg and Fraunhofer IPA, pilot sites, 712 datasets, legs only).
areas.source_short: Unfallchirurgie, 13 Feb 2025 (AMP-Registry update)
areas.since_note: Not stated (predecessor project AMP-Kompass; state funding 2021)

areas.label: Emilia-Romagna Registry of Birth Defects (IMER)
areas.local: Indagine sulle Malformazioni congenite in Emilia-Romagna
areas.area: Whole Emilia-Romagna region, all 22 delivery units, about 100% of births; about 30,000 births a year (30,321 in 2020; 30,406 in 2022).
areas.kind: Population-based regional registry run from the University of Ferrara with the Region; finds cases by linking the regional birth database (CeDAP) and hospital discharge records, and through a clinical network of neonatologists, paediatricians and obstetricians.
areas.source: (1) IMER five-year report 2018-2022, https://salute.regione.emilia-romagna.it/normativa-e-documentazione/rapporti/imer-registro-malformazioni-congenite/report_imer_2024.pdf (PDF text read: years, births 2018-2022, chapter on limb anomalies). (2) EUROCAT member page Emilia Romagna, https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries/Emilia-Romagna_en (history from 1978, coverage, 30,321 births in 2020, last updated 18.04.2023). (3) ICBDSR 2024 annual report (programme page, read 2026-11-22; hosted on a GitHub Pages mirror linked from icbdsr.org), https://ldbotto.github.io/test_icbd/progs/ITAE.html (coverage 100%, limb deficiency counts).
areas.source_short: IMER 5-year report 2018-2022 (May 2024); EUROCAT member page; ICBDSR 2024 report.

areas.label: Congenital Anomalies Registry of the Metropolitan Area of Milan (ATS Milano)
areas.local: Registro delle Malformazioni Congenite dell'Area Metropolitana di Milano
areas.area: Provinces of Milan and Lodi (195 municipalities, about 3.5 million inhabitants), about 30,000 births a year.
areas.kind: Population-based registry in the Epidemiology Unit of the Milan health protection agency; finds cases by linking administrative health flows (hospital discharges, birth certificates, deaths, pathology) and reviewing records.
areas.source: EUROCAT member page Metropolitan Area Milan, https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries/Metropolitan-Area-Milan_en (history, coverage, 81,588 births in 2016, Milan and Lodi provinces); EUROCAT member list https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries_en (Full member).
areas.source_short: EUROCAT member page and list (2026).
areas.since_note: Collection began 2015, established 2016; first birth year 2012; joined EUROCAT 2018

areas.label: Lombardy Congenital Malformations Registry (CMRL), north-west Lombardy
areas.local: Registro Malformazioni Congenite della Lombardia
areas.area: Provinces of Sondrio and Varese and the north of Milan; the programme says about 18.2% of Lombardy's births and 3.1% of Italy's, yet its 2015-2017 table counts only 12,114 births (about 4,040 a year).
areas.kind: Population-based programme; finds cases by algorithms over hospital discharges, death and birth certificates, pathology reports and social-security files, then manual review; includes spontaneous abortions and placental pathology.
areas.source: ICBDSR 2024 annual report (programme page, read 2026-11-22; hosted on a GitHub Pages mirror linked from icbdsr.org), https://ldbotto.github.io/test_icbd/progs/ITAL.html (coverage, data sources, limb deficiency counts); ICBDSR programme directory CSV (programme name 'Italy Lombardy, RMCL').
areas.source_short: ICBDSR 2024 report, programme ITAL; ICBDSR directory.

areas.label: Congenital Anomalies Registry of the Autonomous Province of Trento
areas.local: Registro Anomalie Congenite della Provincia autonoma di Trento
areas.area: Province of Trento; 3,576 births in the province's hospitals in 2024, plus 20 more.
areas.kind: Population-based registry of the provincial health service (clinical epidemiology service, medical genetics, neonatology); finds cases from the birth certificate flow (CedAP), hospital records, prenatal diagnosis and terminations, validated and classified clinically.
areas.source: (1) Rapporto annuale sulle anomalie congenite in provincia di Trento, anno 2024 (PDF read), https://www.epicentro.iss.it/territorio/Trento/pdf/Report_Malformazioni%20congenite_2024.pdf (142 cases, 39.3 per 1,000 births, accreditation to EUROCAT). (2) EUROCAT member list, https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries_en (Full member Trento).
areas.source_short: Trento annual report 2024 (July 2026); EUROCAT list.

areas.label: Congenital Anomalies Registry of ATS Val Padana (Mantova and Cremona)
areas.local: Registro Malformazioni Congenite ATS Val Padana
areas.area: Provinces of Mantova and Cremona (177 municipalities, 755,865 inhabitants), about 5,000 births a year.
areas.kind: Population-based registry in the epidemiology unit of the Val Padana health protection agency; active case search over hospital discharges, outpatient records, birth and death certificates, pathology, prescriptions and the rare diseases registry, with clinical record review.
areas.source: EUROCAT member page Val Padana, https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries/Val-Padana_en (history, coverage, joined EUROCAT 2016, full member 2023); EUROCAT list https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries_en.
areas.source_short: EUROCAT member page and list (2026).
areas.since_note: 2008 (Mantova; first birth year 2002); Cremona added 2021 (first birth year 2016)

areas.label: Veneto Region congenital anomalies programme
areas.local: Registro regionale malformazioni congenite, Regione Veneto
areas.area: Whole Veneto region (4.9 million inhabitants in 2018); about 36,930 births a year in 2015-2018.
areas.kind: Population-based regional programme that integrates hospital discharge records, the regional birth registry and the regional rare disease registry.
areas.source: ICBDSR 2024 annual report (programme page, read 2026-11-22; hosted on a GitHub Pages mirror linked from icbdsr.org), https://ldbotto.github.io/test_icbd/progs/ITAV.html; EUROCAT list https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries_en (Veneto, Affiliate member; page https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries/veneto_en last updated 8.8.2019).
areas.source_short: ICBDSR 2024 report, programme ITAV; EUROCAT list.

areas.label: Apulia Regional Congenital Malformations Registry
areas.local: Registro Malformazioni Congenite della Regione Puglia
areas.area: People born in Apulia and terminations of pregnancy of resident women; regional.
areas.kind: Regional registry set up by Regional Council resolution 1409 of 2013, run by the regional health agency AReSS Puglia (epidemiology and care intelligence).
areas.source: AReSS Puglia page, https://aress.regione.puglia.it/en/aree-tematiche/mappe-e-dati-per-la-salute/registro-malformazioni-congenite (read: 2013 establishment, 2015-2018 data); EUROCAT list https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries_en (Puglia, Affiliate member).
areas.source_short: AReSS Puglia registry page; EUROCAT list.

areas.local: Registro Nazionale Malformazioni Congenite
areas.area: National; collects regional data through a web platform for the regions that asked for it. Participating regions are not named on the page.
areas.kind: Population-based national registry at the National Centre for Rare Diseases of the Istituto Superiore di Sanita, modelled on EUROCAT; regional registries upload cases diagnosed prenatally, at birth and up to one year.

areas.source_short: ISS RNMC page (updated Jan 2022).
areas.since_note: Set up under a 2017 Ministry of Health project; page published Feb 2020

areas.label: Spanish Collaborative Study of Congenital Malformations (ECEMC)
areas.local: Estudio Colaborativo Espanol de Malformaciones Congenitas
areas.area: About 45 hospitals across Spain; about 50,000 births a year, around 15% of Spanish births.
areas.kind: Hospital-based case-control surveillance programme at the Institute of Rare Diseases Research, Carlos III Health Institute; physicians record defects seen in the first 3 days of life and interview the mothers.
areas.source: EUROCAT member page ECEMC, https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries/Hospital%20Network%20%28ECEMC%29_en (history, 45 hospitals, 50,000 births); EUROCAT list https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries_en; ICBDSR programme directory CSV ('Spain, ECEMC').
areas.source_short: EUROCAT member page; ICBDSR directory.

areas.label: Population-based Registry of Congenital Anomalies of the Valencian Community
areas.local: Registro Poblacional de Anomalias Congenitas de la Comunitat Valenciana
areas.area: Whole Valencian Community, about 5 million people, about 40,000 births a year.
areas.kind: Population-based registry run by FISABIO and the regional public health directorate; all major anomalies in pregnancies of resident mothers, with stillbirths from 22 weeks.
areas.source: (1) FISABIO report 2007-2023, https://fisabio.san.gva.es/media/upload/arxius/salud-publica/enfermedades-raras/informe-web-ac-2026.pdf (PDF read: title, Jan 2026, EUROCAT full member). (2) EUROCAT member page, https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries/Valencia-Region_en (population, births).
areas.source_short: FISABIO report 2007-2023 (Jan 2026); EUROCAT member page.
areas.since_note: Pilot 2010, data collected retrospectively from 2007; EUROCAT full member since 2011

areas.label: Congenital Anomalies Registry of Navarra (RACEHNA)
areas.local: Registro de Anomalias Congenitas de Navarra
areas.area: Navarre, about 600,000 inhabitants, about 6,000 births a year.
areas.kind: Population-based registry officially established by Foral Order 69/2013.
areas.source: EUROCAT member page, https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries/navarra_en; EUROCAT list https://eu-rd-platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/eurocat/eurocat-members/registries_en.
areas.source_short: EUROCAT member page and list.

areas.label: Congenital Anomalies Registry of Aragon (ARACA)
areas.local: Registro de Anomalias Congenitas de Aragon
areas.area: Aragon, about 1.3 million inhabitants; expanding from one hospital to the whole region.

areas.source_short: Nemours ILDR listing; NHS HRA summary; UBC Orthopaedics
